content:
The image shows a soybean stem with a white, cottony/fluffy mycelial growth covering it. The stem appears bleached/white with visible fluffy fungal mycelium. Some lower leaves appear wilted/brown. The pods nearby look healthy but the stem is clearly infected.

This is classic White Mold (caused by *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*) — characterized by:
- White, cottony mycelium on the stem
- Bleached/white stem tissue
- Fluffy fungal growth wrapping the stem
- Wilting/dying tissue below the infected area

No other soybean disease presents with this distinctive white cottony stem growth.
